item.title: Katsuren Castle Ruins — Guide
item.description: Katsuren Castle (Katsuren-jo), on a hill on the Katsuren Peninsula in central Okinawa, is one of the island’s oldest gusuku (Ryukyu castles) and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for its commanding hilltop position and superb panoramic views. Dating to around the 13th–14th centuries, it was the seat of the powerful and ambitious lord Amawari, whose prosperity through overseas trade made Katsuren a thriving centre — a history dramatically underlined in 2016 when archaeologists discovered ancient Roman and Ottoman coins among the ruins, hinting at the reach of Ryukyu’s trade networks.

item.title: Nakagusuku Castle Ruins — Guide
item.description: Nakagusuku Castle (Nakagusuku-jo) is one of the best-preserved of Okinawa’s gusuku (Ryukyu castles) and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, spread across a ridge in central Okinawa with commanding views. Built in stages up to the 15th century and associated with the renowned lord Gosamaru, the castle is celebrated for the beauty and sophistication of its curving limestone walls, which sweep gracefully along the contours of the hilltop and showcase several styles of Ryukyuan stone-fitting technique.

item.title: Nakijin Castle Ruins — Guide
item.description: Nakijin Castle (Nakijin-jo), on the Motobu Peninsula in northern Okinawa, is one of the island’s largest and most impressive gusuku (Ryukyu castle) ruins and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Once the stronghold of the kings of Hokuzan, one of the three kingdoms that divided Okinawa before its 15th-century unification, the castle sprawls across a scenic hilltop, its long, undulating stone walls winding for hundreds of metres along the ridgeline and commanding sweeping views over the surrounding forest and the sea.

item.title: Ryukyu Gusuku Guide: Zakimi Castle & UNESCO Ruins
item.description: Long before Shuri unified the islands, Okinawa was dotted with gusuku — the fortified castles of rival Ryukyu lords. Several of their dramatic ruins, prized for their flowing, beautifully engineered curved limestone walls, are inscribed together as UNESCO World Heritage (“Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu”). Zakimi Castle in Yomitan is among the most accessible and best preserved, its ramparts open to walk and offering views to the sea.
